en.title: The Climate Change Department conducts a CRVA Validation Workshop in Fuvahmulah City
en.description: The Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy conducted a Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessment (CRVA) sharing workshop in Fuvahmulah City under the Advancing the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) of the Maldives project, bringing together stakeholders to share the findings and strengthen…
en.body:
The Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy conducted a Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessment (CRVA) sharing workshop in Fuvahmulah City under the Advancing the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) of the Maldives project, bringing together stakeholders to share the findings and strengthen locally informed climate adaptation planning for the city. The workshop was opened by remarks from the Fuvahmulah City Council Mayor, Ismail Rafeeq and the Climate Change Department’s Director, Thibyan Ibrahim.

The workshop featured presentations on the NAP process and the climate risk and vulnerability assessment findings by Senior Climate Change Adaptation Consultant from the NAP Global Network, Jauza Khaleel and climate change expert, Mareer Mohamed Husny. The Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessment presented during the workshop highlighted key climate hazards, including flooding, coastal erosion, and swell wave impacts, based on local consultations and technical analysis. The session also examined existing adaptation responses such as stormwater management systems, flood gates, mangrove planting, and emergency response measures, while gathering stakeholder feedback to validate local climate risk priorities and identify practical pathways for strengthening resilience.

Held as part of the Maldives’ ongoing efforts to strengthen national adaptation planning, the workshop forms part of the Green Climate Fund-funded NAP readiness project, implemented by the Ministry with support from the United Nations Environment Programme. The project aims to strengthen institutional coordination for adaptation planning, improve evidence-based decision-making, enhance private sector engagement, and mobilize adaptation finance to support long-term climate resilience planning in the Maldives.

The workshop was supported by the following officials from the Climate Change Department: Principal Environment Management Officer Fathimath Zaina Shareef, Senior Environment Management Officer Ahmed Masoon Hassan and Senior Environment Management Officer Raniya Husnu Al Suood, NAP Project Administrative and Finance Officer Hawwa Dhaiba, Izman Suhail Climate Adaptation Analyst and Climate Change Expert Aishath Aileen Niyaz.

en.title: The Climate Change Department conducts a stakeholder consultation in Fuvahmulah City
en.description: Stakeholder consultation sessions were held in Fuvahmulah City on 13th May 2026 under the Third National Communication project of the Maldives, supported by UNEP. The sessions brought together stakeholders from the agriculture and tourism sectors to discuss the impacts of climate change on their…
en.body:
Stakeholder consultation sessions were held in Fuvahmulah City on 13th May 2026 under the Third National Communication project of the Maldives, supported by UNEP. The sessions brought together stakeholders from the agriculture and tourism sectors to discuss the impacts of climate change on their respective sectors and to gather their views and experiences.

National Communications submitted under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change provide information on national circumstances, climate impacts, adaptation efforts, and other measures taken to address climate change. The consultations held in Fuvahmulah will contribute to the development of the adaptation chapter of the Maldives’ Third National Communication by incorporating sector-specific stakeholder perspectives and information.

Discussions focused on the impacts, challenges, and losses faced by the agriculture and tourism sectors as a result of climate change, as well as the need for practical and locally informed adaptation measures. Input gathered through the sessions will help strengthen the national assessment of vulnerabilities and adaptation needs, while also supporting the development of proposals to access climate finance for vulnerable sectors.

These consultations were conducted by Thibyan Ibrahim, Fathimath Zaina Shareef, Ahmed Masoon Hassan, Raniya Husnu Al Suood, and Hawwa Daiba from the Climate Change Department and supported by Gasith Mohammed (NDC Partnership), Jauza Khaleel (NAP-GN) , Izman Suhail (Commonwealth) Aishath Aileen Niyaz (Climate Change Expert).

en.title: Minister Ali Shareef takes part in the “Türkiye’s Road to COP31: Resilient Cities”
en.description: Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy, H.E. Mr. Ali Shareef, represented the Maldives at the high-level event “Türkiye’s Road to COP31: Resilient Cities”, held from 8–9 May 2026 in Hatay, Türkiye. He was accompanied by Director, Mr. Thibyan Ibrahim from the Climate Change Department of…
en.body:
Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy, H.E. Mr. Ali Shareef, represented the Maldives at the high-level event *“Türkiye’s Road to COP31: Resilient Cities”*, held from 8–9 May 2026 in Hatay, Türkiye. He was accompanied by Director, Mr. Thibyan Ibrahim from the Climate Change Department of the Ministry.

The event convened ministers, policymakers, and international stakeholders to advance dialogue on climate-resilient urban development in the lead-up to COP31, with a strong focus on post-disaster recovery as an opportunity to build sustainable, inclusive, and resilient cities.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/20260517-pic-minister-ali-shareef-takes-part-in-the-trkiyes-road-to-cop31-resilient-cities-1.png)

During the High-Level Special Session titled *“From the Disaster of the Century to the Construction of Sustainable Cities,”* Minister Ali Shareef emphasized on the importance of global cooperation in advancing the shared vision of resilient and climate-adaptive development. In his intervention, the Minister highlighted that the Maldives’ Third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and the forthcoming National Adaptation Plan are closely aligned with the Maldives Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy (2024–2030). He emphasized that these frameworks collectively strengthen the integration of disaster risk reduction priorities, including the enhancement of early warning systems, the protection of critical coastal ecosystems such as coral reefs and mangroves, and the promotion of climate-resilient infrastructure. Minister also reaffirmed Maldives’ strong support for Türkiye’s leadership as the incoming COP31 Presidency.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/20260517-pic-minister-ali-shareef-takes-part-in-the-trkiyes-road-to-cop31-resilient-cities-4.png)

Minister Ali Shareef also participated in the Ministerial Roundtable, where he stressed the urgent need to embed disaster risk reduction and climate resilience into long-term national development planning. He noted that disaster risk reduction is systematically integrated across all climate policies in Maldives and is aligned with the national roadmap to achieve the United Nations Secretary-General’s Early Warnings for All Initiative. He further highlighted that these considerations are being incorporated into the upcoming National Adaptation Plan to ensure risk-informed decision-making at all levels of governance.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/20260517-pic-minister-ali-shareef-takes-part-in-the-trkiyes-road-to-cop31-resilient-cities-3.png)

On the sidelines of the event, Minister Ali Shareef held a bilateral meeting with Minister of Environment, Urabanisation and Climate Change from Türkiye, H.E. Mr. Murat Kurum the incoming COP31 President. Minister Ali Shareef also held bilateral meetings with ministers from Bangladesh, Brunei, Libya and Kosovo, and the Executive Director of UN HABITAT to strengthen cooperation on climate action and resilience-building efforts.

featuredImage.alt: Maldives Participated at the High-Level Opening of the First Conference on Transiting Away from Fossil

en.title: Maldives Participated at the High-Level Opening of the First Conference on Transiting Away from Fossil
en.description: On 28 April 2026, the Maldives participated in the First Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels in Santa Marta, Colombia, and was represented by the State Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy, H.E. Ibrahim Mimrah. Co-hosted by the governments of Colombia and the…
en.body:
On 28 April 2026, the Maldives participated in the First Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels in Santa Marta, Colombia, and was represented by the State Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy, H.E. Ibrahim Mimrah. Co-hosted by the governments of Colombia and the Netherlands, the Conference brought together countries and other stakeholders to advance practical pathways for a just, orderly, and equitable transition away from fossil fuels, in line with climate goals and the best available science.

In his national statement, State Minister Mimrah highlighted the challenges arising from the Maldives’ structural dependence on imported fuels, which exposes the country to volatility in global prices and supply disruptions, with direct impacts on economic stability and livelihoods. He emphasized, “Our challenge is not fossil fuel production; it is fossil fuel dependence.” He further stressed that transitioning to renewable energy will require transformation across the entire energy system, and that achieving renewable energy targets will depend on investment in key enablers, including modern grids, storage, energy management systems, decentralized solutions, and resilient infrastructure.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260429-First-Conference-2.png)

Access to finance remains one of the greatest barriers for Small Island Developing States (SIDS). In this regard, the state minister called for concessional financing and, where possible, grant-based climate finance free from undue conditionalities and without adding to existing debt burdens. He emphasized that climate finance must support, not dictate, nationally determined transition pathways. Reaffirming the Maldives’ commitment to a just and inclusive energy transition, State Minister Mimrah called for enhanced international cooperation grounded in equity to ensure that no one is left behind.

On the sidelines of the Conference, the Maldivian delegation also held bilateral meetings with other countries to strengthen cooperation in support of the Maldives’ transition to a low-emission and climate-resilient future

featuredImage.alt: Knowledge-Sharing Workshop on Coastal Studies and Resilient Design for Kulhudhuffushi City’s East Coast

en.title: Knowledge-Sharing Workshop on Coastal Studies and Resilient Design for Kulhudhuffushi City’s East Coast
en.description: The Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy (MoCCEE) has conducted a one-day knowledge-sharing workshop to present the findings of marine and coastal studies carried out along the eastern shoreline of Hdh. Kulhudhuffushi. The workshop forms part of the Marine and Coastal Modeling and…
en.body:
The Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy (MoCCEE) has conducted a one-day knowledge-sharing workshop to present the findings of marine and coastal studies carried out along the eastern shoreline of Hdh. Kulhudhuffushi. The workshop forms part of the Marine and Coastal Modeling and Detailed Design Study under the Enhancing Climate Resilience and Food Security Project (ECRFSP). The study is being implemented by Land and Marine Environmental Resource (LAMER) Group Pvt Ltd as the technical consultancy.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/M3_4.png)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/M3_1.png)

The workshop was officially inaugurated by the Minister of State for MoCCEE, Mr. Abdulla Ziyad, who highlighted the significance of the work undertaken to collect state-of-the-art, high-resolution, and seasonally representative data over a one-year period. He noted that this data enables the development of robust, evidence-based designs for climate-resilient infrastructure. He also commended the stakeholder and community consultations conducted in collaboration with the Kulhudhuffushi City Council and relevant national agencies, ensuring that local knowledge is effectively integrated into data analysis and design outcomes.

The workshop sessions provided a comprehensive overview of the project and study area, including key challenges, risks, user groups, stakeholders, and existing land use. Presentations also covered critical coastal processes affecting Kulhudhuffushi, such as sediment transport, shoreline morphology, and erosion patterns. In addition, a range of modelling analyses were shared, including downscaled extreme wave assessments, beach overtopping and flood threshold studies with hazard mapping, as well as hydrodynamic and morphodynamic modelling. These findings have been synthesized to inform risk reduction and climate adaptation strategies, leading to the development of draft concept designs for a more resilient east coast.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/M3_5.png)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/M3_6.png)

A total of 45 participants attended the hybrid workshop, representing technical experts from relevant government institutions and private sector stakeholders. Participants provided valuable feedback on the coastal studies, flood hazard maps, and proposed concept designs, contributing to the identification of a balanced approach that combines sustainable infrastructure and nature-based solutions to mitigate flood risks and strengthen coastal protection in the area.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/M3_3.png)

The overarching goal of ECRFSP is to reduce the vulnerability of Maldivian island communities to climate risks by strengthening both institutional and community capacities. Under Output 2 of the project, two key studies are being conducted in Kulhudhuffushi city. The Inland Hydrology Modeling and Detailed Design Study focuses on areas prone to pluvial flooding and the island’s mangrove wetlands, while the Marine and Coastal Modeling and Detailed Design Study addresses coastal dynamics and shoreline protection.

The project is financed through a combination of grants, loans, and technical assistance from the Asian Development Fund, the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific, the Ocean Resilience Coastal Adaptation Trust Fund, and the Government of Maldives.

en.title: Community Workshops in Kulhudhuffushi City to Gather Public Input on Resilient East Coast Designs
en.description: A series of stakeholder and community workshops have been held in Hdh. Kulhudhuffushi to help guide the development of conceptual designs for the city’s eastern coastline. The workshops form part of the Marine and Coastal Modeling and Detailed Design Study under the Enhancing Climate Resilience and…
en.body:
![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Community-session-1-300x169.png)

A series of stakeholder and community workshops have been held in Hdh. Kulhudhuffushi to help guide the development of conceptual designs for the city’s eastern coastline. The workshops form part of the Marine and Coastal Modeling and Detailed Design Study under the Enhancing Climate Resilience and Food Security Project (ECRFSP), implemented by the Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy. The study is being carried out by Land and Marine Environmental Resource (LAMER) Group Pvt Ltd as the technical consultancy.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Stakeholder-session-300x169.png)

Since the study commenced in June 2025, extensive field surveys and island-wide numerical modelling have been undertaken. These efforts have led to the preparation of draft concept designs aimed at strengthening the resilience of Kulhudhuffushi’s east coast. A key objective of the study is to identify a combination of infrastructure and nature-based solutions to address flood risks and enhance coastal protection in the area.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Community-session-2-300x240.jpeg)

Earlier consultations with key stakeholders, held in September 2025, focused on gathering community perspectives on potential solutions to the challenges faced along the eastern shoreline. Building on this, the recent workshops were designed to capture stakeholder and community feedback on coastal studies, flood hazard maps, and the proposed concept designs. The insights gathered will help refine sustainable, community-supported coastal management approaches. A total of 39 participants took part in these consultation sessions.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Gender-session-4-300x169.png)![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Gender-session-1-300x169.png)

In addition, a dedicated gender session was conducted with 25 female participants, including incoming and outgoing members of the Women’s Development Committee (WDC), as well as representatives and staff of the City Council, to provide orientation on the requirements of the project’s Gender Action Plan (GAP).

The session highlighted the critical role of women in climate resilience, disaster planning, and food security, while also exploring opportunities to further strengthen their participation and leadership in these areas.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Gender-session-2-300x169.png)![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Gender-Session-3-300x169.png)![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Gender-5-300x169.png)

Through evidence-based discussion and participant reflection, the session reemphasized that women are central to building climate resilience and strengthening food security in the Maldives. It further emphasized the value of continued engagement to ensure women’s meaningful participation throughout the implementation of the project.

The overarching goal of ECRFSP is to reduce the vulnerability of Maldivian island communities to climate risks by strengthening both institutional and community capacities. Under Output 2 of the project, two key studies are being conducted in Kulhudhuffushi. The Inland Hydrology Modeling and Detailed Design Study focuses on areas prone to pluvial flooding and the island’s mangrove wetlands, while the Marine and Coastal Modeling and Detailed Design Study addresses coastal dynamics and shoreline protection.

The project is financed through a combination of grants, loans, and technical assistance from the Asian Development Fund, the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific, the Ocean Resilience Coastal Adaptation Trust Fund, and the Government of Maldives.

featuredImage.alt: President Appoints Ali Shareef as Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy

en.title: President Appoints Ali Shareef as Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy
en.description: President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu has officially appointed Mr. Ali Shareef as the Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy.
en.body:
President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu has officially appointed Mr. Ali Shareef as the Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy.

The appointment ceremony was held today at the President’s Office, where Mr. Ali Shareef took his oath of office. Following the appointment, the President presented him with the Letter of Appointment.

Mr. Ali Shareef brings extensive experience to the role, particularly in the fields of climate policy, environmental management and renewable energy. His leadership is expected to be pivotal as the Maldives continues to advocate for climate justice on the global stage and works toward achieving its ambitious renewable energy targets for 2028.

dv.title: މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ކްލައިމެޓް ޗޭންޖް، އެންވަޔަރަންމަންޓް އެންޑް އެނަރޖީގެ މަޤާމަށް އަލީ ޝަރީފް އައްޔަންކުރައްވައިފި
dv.description: މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ކްލައިމެޓް ޗޭންޖް، އެންވަޔަރަންމަންޓް އެންޑް އެނަރޖީގެ މަޤާމަށް އަލްފާޟިލް ޢަލީ ޝަރީފް، ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒު މިއަދު އައްޔަންކުރައްވައިފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ކްލައިމެޓް ޗޭންޖް، އެންވަޔަރަންމަންޓް އެންޑް އެނަރޖީގެ މަޤާމަށް އަލްފާޟިލް ޢަލީ ޝަރީފް، ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒު މިއަދު އައްޔަންކުރައްވައިފިއެވެ.

މި މަޤާމަށް އޭނާ އައްޔަންކުރެއްވުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތު އޮތީ މިއަދު ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ އޮފީހުގައެވެ. މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ޢަލީ ޝަރީފް ވަނީ ވަޒީރުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ މެންބަރެއްގެ ހައިސިއްޔަތުން މަޤާމުގެ ހުވާ ކުރައްވާފައެވެ. ހުވައި ލައިދެއްވީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އުއްތަމަ ފަނޑިޔާރު އޮނަރަބަލް އަލްއުސްތާޛު ޢަބްދުލްޣަނީ މުޙައްމަދެވެ.  ހުވައި ކުރެއްވުމަށްފަހު، ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ވަނީ އޭނާއަށް މަޤާމުގެ ފަތްކޮޅު އަރުވާފައެވެ.

ޢަލީ ޝަރީފަކީ މޫސުމީ ބަދަލުތަކާއި ތިމާވެށީގެ ދާއިރާއިން ގިނަ ތަޖުރިބާތަކެއް ހާސިލުކުރައްވާފައިވާ ބޭފުޅެކެވެ. ރާއްޖޭގެ ތިމާވެށި ހިމާޔަތްކުރުމާއި، އިއާދަކުރަނިވި ހަކަތައިގެ އަމާޒުތައް ހާސިލުކުރުމުގައި އަލީ ޝަރީފް ވަނީ އިސްދައުރެއް އަދާކޮށްފައެވެ.

featuredImage.alt: Maldives Hosts Three-Day Forum on Climate-Induced Water Security for Atoll Nations

en.title: Maldives Hosts Three-Day Forum on Climate-Induced Water Security for Atoll Nations
en.description: The Government of Maldives, through the Climate Change Department of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment, has officially inaugurated the “Climate-Induced Water Security in Atoll Nations Forum,” held from 7th to 9th April 2026 at Barceló Nasandhura Malé. The forum is convened by the Ministry of…
en.body:
The Government of Maldives, through the Climate Change Department of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment, has officially inaugurated the “Climate-Induced Water Security in Atoll Nations Forum,” held from 7th to 9th April 2026 at Barceló Nasandhura Malé. The forum is convened by the Ministry of Tourism and Environment in its capacity as Chair of the Coalition of Atoll Nations on Climate Change (CANCC).

The three-day forum brings together representatives from atoll nations, development partners, and key stakeholders to address the growing challenges of water security driven by climate change and to identify resilient and sustainable solutions for vulnerable island communities. The forum is organized with support from the Green Climate Fund (GCF) Readiness Project, “Strengthening the Water Sector for Enhanced Planning, Programming and Implementation of Climate Finance in the Republic of Maldives,” in collaboration with the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ).

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-8.png)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-10.png)

Participants include representatives from Kiribati, Tuvalu, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and Tokelau, alongside local utilities, regulatory bodies, academia, and technical experts. The forum provides a vital platform for dialogue on one of the most pressing challenges facing low-lying island states, namely water security in the face of climate change.

The forum was officially opened by the Minister of Tourism and Environment, H.E. Thoriq Ibrahim, who highlighted the growing vulnerability of Small Island Developing States to climate-induced water stress. In his remarks, the Minister underscored the profound environmental changes already being experienced across the Maldives and similar island contexts. He noted that rainfall patterns are becoming increasingly unpredictable, dry periods are intensifying, and saltwater intrusion is contaminating fragile freshwater lenses. These changes, he emphasized, are not distant threats but present-day realities already affecting communities across the country.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-4.png)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-3.png)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-2.png)

He further stated that the Government of Maldives has placed water security at the center of its climate agenda. Through its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0), the country has committed to strengthening climate resilience while advancing low-carbon development. Achieving water security, as emphasized during the forum, requires integrated approaches that combine infrastructure investment, technological innovation, and community-based adaptation strategies. The Maldives continues to invest significantly in these areas, prioritizing climate-resilient infrastructure, improved water management systems, and sustainable resource use.

The forum included a series of technical exchange sessions, providing a platform for participants to share knowledge and practical experiences across atoll nations. These sessions focused on key thematic areas such as desalination and water production systems, groundwater management and protection, rainwater harvesting, utility operations and maintenance, and emergency water preparedness. Experts from government agencies, utilities, and development partners contributed valuable insights into both the challenges and solutions relevant to small island and atoll environments.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-6.png)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-7.png)

dv.title: “ކްލައިމެޓް އިންޑިއުސްޑް ވޯޓަރ ސެކިއުރިޓީ ފޯރަމް” ފަށައިފި
dv.description: މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން ފެނުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން ކަށަވަރުކުރުމަށް ކުރިމަތިވާ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކުރުމަށް ބާއްވާ “ކްލައިމެޓް އިންޑިއުސްޑް ވޯޓަރ ސެކިއުރިޓީ ފޯރަމް” މިއަދު މާލޭގައި ފަށައިފިއެވެ. މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ޓޫރިޒަމް އެންޑް އެންވަޔަރަންމަންޓުން އިންތިޒާމުކުރާ މި ފޯރަމަކީ…
dv.body:
މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން ފެނުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން ކަށަވަރުކުރުމަށް ކުރިމަތިވާ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކުރުމަށް ބާއްވާ “ކްލައިމެޓް އިންޑިއުސްޑް ވޯޓަރ ސެކިއުރިޓީ ފޯރަމް” މިއަދު މާލޭގައި ފަށައިފިއެވެ. މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ޓޫރިޒަމް އެންޑް އެންވަޔަރަންމަންޓުން އިންތިޒާމުކުރާ މި ފޯރަމަކީ ގްރީން ކްލައިމެޓް ފަންޑް (ޖީ.ސީ.އެފް) އަދި ޖަރުމަނުގެ ޖީ.އައި.ޒެޑް (GIZ)  އާ ގުޅިގެން ތިން ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަށް ކުރިއަށްގެންދާ ބައްދަލުވުމެކެވެ.

މިފޯރަމްގައި ރާއްޖޭގެ އިތުރުން ދެން ބައިވެރިވަނީ މުރަކައިގެ މައްޗައް އެކުލެވޭ ކުދިޖަޒީރާ ގައުމުތައް ކަމުގައިވާ ކިރިބާސް، ޓުވާލޫ، ރިޕަބްލިކް އޮފް މާޝަލް އައިލެންޑްސް، އަދި ޓޮކެލާކޫ އެވެ. މިގައުމުތަކުގެ ޕޮލިސީ، ރެގިއުލޭޓަރީ، ތައުލީމީ، ފަންނީ އަދި ޔުޓިލިޓީ ޚިދުމަތްދޭ ފަރާތްތަކުން ބައިވެރިވެއެވެ. މިއީ ފެނުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން ކަށަވަރުކުރުމަށް ހުރި ގޮންޖެހުންތަކާ މެދު ދިވެހި ރާއްޖެއާ އެއްފަދަ ކުދިޖަޒީރާ ގައުމުތަކުގެ މެދުގައި މަޝްވަރާ ކުރުމަށް ބޭއްވޭ ބައްދަކުވުމެކެވެ.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-5.png)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-10.png)

މި ފޯރަމް ރަސްމީކޮށް ހުޅުއްވައިދެއްވީ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ޓޫރިޒަމް އެންޑް އެންވަޔަރަންމަންޓް، ތާރިގް އިބްރާހީމެވެ. އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ ވާހަކަފުޅުގައި، މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން ތަރައްގީވަމުން އަންނަ ކުދި ޖަޒީރާ ގައުމުތަކަށް ފެނުގެ ދަތިކަން ކުރިމަތިވުމުގެ ފުރުސަތު ބޮޑުވަމުންދާކަން ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި ރާއްޖެއާއި މިފަދަ އެހެން ޖަޒީރާ ގައުމުތަކަށް މިހާރުވެސް ތަހައްމަލު ކުރަންޖެހިފައިވާ ތިމާވެށީގެ ބޮޑެތި ބަދަލުތަކުގެ މައްޗަށް އަލިއަޅުއްވާލެއްވިއެވެ. އެގޮތުން، ވާރޭ ވެހޭގޮތްތަކަށް ބަދަލު އައުމާއި، ވާރޭނުވެހޭދުވަސްވަރު ދިގުލައިގެން ދިއުމާއިލޮނުވަނުމުގެ ސަބަބުން ބިމުގެ ފެންފަށަލަ ލޮނުން ތަޣައްޔަރުވުން ހިމެނެއެވެ.

އިތުރަށް ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުން މިނިސްޓަރު ވިދާޅުވީ، ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން ފެނުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން ކަށަވަރުކުރުމަށް ވަރަށް ބޮޑު އިސްކަމެއް ދީފައިވާ ކަމަށެވެ. ރާއްޖޭގެ ކްލައިމެޓް އެކްޝަން ޕްލޭންގައި ވާފަދައިން ކާބަން މަދުވާނެގޮތަށް ތަރައްޤީގެ މަޝްރޫއުތައް ބައްޓަންކުރުމާއި މޫސުމީ ވިލުންތެރިކަން ވަރުގަދަކުރުމަށް ދިވެހި ރާއްޖޭން ވަނީ ކަނޑައަޅާފައެވެ. ފޯރަމްގައި ފާހަގަކުރެވުނު ގޮތުގައި، ފެނުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން ކަށަވަރުކުރުމަށް ކަށަވަރުކުރުމަށްޓަކައި އިންފްރާސްޓްރަކްޗަރ އަށް އިންވެސްޓްކުރުމާއި، ޓެކްނޮލޮޖީގެ އައު އީޖާދުތަކާއި، އަދި މުޖުތަމައުގެ ބައިވެރިވުން ހިމެނޭހެން ޝާމިލުވާ އުސޫލުތަކެއް ބޭނުންވެއެވެ. ރާއްޖެއިން ދަނީ މި ދާއިރާތަކަށް ބޮޑެތި އިންވެސްޓްމަންޓްތައް ކުރަމުންކަމަށް ވެސް މިނިސްޓަރ ވިދާޅުވުވިއެވެ.

މި ފޯރަމްގައި ކުރިއަށްދާ ފަންނީ ސެޝަންތަކުގައި، ބައިވެރިވާ ގައުމުތަކުގެ މެދުގައި މައުލޫމާތާއި އަމަލީ ތަޖުރިބާ ހިއްސާކުރުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވެއެވެ. މި ސެޝަންތަކުގައި މައިގަނޑު ގޮތެއްގައި އަލިއަޅުއްވާލާފައިވަނީ ލޮނުފެން މީރުފެނަށް ހަދާ ނިޒާމުތައް، ބިންމުގެ ފެންފަށަލަ މެނޭޖްކުރުމާއި ރައްކާތެރިކުރުން ، ވާރޭފެން ނެގުމާއި ރައްކާކުރުން، ޔުޓިލިޓީ އޮޕަރޭޝަންތަކާއި މަރާމާތު އަދި ކުއްލި ހާލަތްތަކުގައި ފެން ފޯރުކޮށްދިނުމުގެ މައްޗަށެވެ.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-7.png)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260407-CANCC-Water-Security-6.png)

featuredImage.alt: High-Level Dialogue and Stakeholder Engagement Workshop: Joint Initiatives of SOFF-Funded UNEP Investment Phase and GCF TRACT Project

en.title: High-Level Dialogue and Stakeholder Engagement Workshop: Joint Initiatives of SOFF-Funded UNEP Investment Phase and GCF TRACT Project
en.description: On 30 March 2026, the Climate Change Department of Ministry of Tourism and Environment and Maldives Meteorological Service co-hosted a High-Level Dialogue and Stakeholder Engagement Workshop in Male’, bringing together government institutions, development partners, technical experts, and…
en.body:
On 30 March 2026, the Climate Change Department of Ministry of Tourism and Environment and Maldives Meteorological Service co-hosted a High-Level Dialogue and Stakeholder Engagement Workshop in Male’, bringing together government institutions, development partners, technical experts, and stakeholders from across sectors. The event focused on advancing the joint implementation of the Systematic Observations Financing Facility (SOFF)-Funded UNEP Investment Phase and the GCF TRACT Project, both of which are central to strengthening national climate resilience and early warning systems.

The workshop provided a platform to enhance coordination, share knowledge, and build a common understanding of how climate data and early warning systems can better support decision-making and disaster preparedness across the country.

The workshop opened with remarks from the Minister of State for Tourism and Environment Mr. Ibrahim Mimrah, highlighting the Maldives’ continued commitment to climate resilience, particularly through investments in multi-hazard early warning systems and strengthened climate data infrastructure.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/20260330-Tract-SOFF-highlevel.png)

Opening remarks was also given by the UN Resident Coordinator to the Maldives Mr. Hao Zhang who reflected on the importance of enhancing early warning systems in the Maldives to address growing concerns on the impacts of climate change.

One of the components of the dialogue was the implementation of the SOFF-funded UNEP Investment Phase, which aims to enhance national meteorological and observational capacity in alignment with the Global Basic Observing Network (GBON).

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/20260330-Tract-SOFF-highlevel-6.png)

Technical discussions explored:

* The current status and future direction of early warning systems in the Maldives
* Opportunities and challenges in strengthening meteorological infrastructure
* The application of climate data for sectoral planning and decision-making
* International experiences and good practices in weather and climate services

Participants also examined how improved climate information can support preparedness for priority risks such as flooding, coastal erosion, and extreme weather events.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/20260330-Tract-SOFF-highlevel-5.png)

A dedicated stakeholder session enabled participants to share insights on the use and requirements of climate data across sectors. Discussions highlighted the importance of:

* Strengthening coordination between institutions
* Improving data sharing and integration
* Ensuring that early warning information reaches communities effectively

The workshop reinforced the need for more integrated and collaborative approaches to climate resilience, moving beyond sector-specific planning.

The workshop also marked the official inception of the GCF TRACT Project, supported by the Green Climate Fund. The project aims to enhance climate resilience through strengthened early warning systems and institutional capacity.

The session introduced:

* The project’s objectives, scope, and implementation approach
* Linkages with ongoing Early Warnings for All (EW4ALL) initiatives
* Contributions from key national stakeholders, including NDMA, MRC and CAM.

The workshop was closed by the Director of Climate Change Department Mr. Ahmed Waheed who highlighted the collaborative effort it took to get projects such as TRACT approved as well as the importance of climate finance for adaptation actions for countries like the Maldives.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/20260330-Tract-SOFF-highlevel-4.png)

As a Small Island Developing State highly vulnerable to climate change, the Maldives continues to prioritize investments in climate data, early warning systems, and institutional capacity. The joint implementation of the SOFF UNEP Investment Phase and the GCF TRACT Project represents an important step toward building a more climate-resilient, data-driven, and prepared nation, ensuring that communities are better equipped to anticipate and respond to climate-related risks.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/20260330-Tract-SOFF-highlevel-3.png)

featuredImage.alt: Initial Consultation Held to Develop GCF Project Concept for Education Sector

en.title: Initial Consultation Held to Develop GCF Project Concept for Education Sector
en.description: The Climate Change Department of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment, in partnership with Ministry of Education and UNICEF, convened the “GCF Project Proposal – Initial Stakeholder Workshop” on 15 February 2026 at Meeruma, Malé.
en.body:
The Climate Change Department of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment, in partnership with Ministry of Education and UNICEF, convened the *“GCF Project Proposal – Initial Stakeholder Workshop”* on 15 February 2026 at Meeruma, Malé.

The workshop brought together representatives from relevant government institutions and technical partners to initiate discussions on developing a project concept for submission to the Green Climate Fund (GCF). The session forms part of ongoing efforts to strengthen the Maldives’ country pipeline to the GCF and mobilise climate finance for priority adaptation needs.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260215-pic-gcfunicef-workshop-5-1024x819.jpeg)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260215-pic-gcfunicef-workshop-1-1024x820.jpeg)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260215-pic-gcfunicef-workshop-4-1024x819.jpeg)

The workshop commenced with opening remarks by His Excellency Dr. Ahmed Mohamed, State Minister for Education, followed by remarks from UNICEF Representative Dr. Edward Addai and Director General of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment, Mr. Amjad Abdulla. During the opening segment, all speakers emphasised the importance of integrating climate resilience into critical public infrastructure, particularly within the education sector, and highlighted the need for coordinated stakeholder engagement in the early stages of project development.

During the technical sessions, participants reviewed the initial Project Ideation Note, including the proposed problem statement, theory of change, and indicative results framework. Discussions focused on identifying priority vulnerabilities, refining potential interventions, and ensuring alignment with national climate policies, sector strategies, and GCF investment criteria.

The proposed concept under discussion seeks to strengthen climate resilience in schools by enhancing institutional frameworks, promoting climate-smart and energy-efficient infrastructure, and integrating adaptation measures that support both students and surrounding communities during climate-related emergencies.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260215-pic-gcfunicef-workshop-6-1024x819.jpeg)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260215-pic-gcfunicef-workshop-3-1024x819.jpeg)

Participants engaged in discussions to provide inputs on implementation arrangements, institutional roles and responsibilities, financing structures, safeguards, and next steps in the proposal development process. The workshop concluded with agreement on timelines and coordination mechanisms to further refine the concept for submission to the GCF. His Excellency Dr. Abdul Latheef Mohamed, Minister of State for Education, closed the workshop by thanking participants and highlighting the important of moving forward with the proposal.

This proposal is being developed by the Climate Change Department of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment with support from UNICEF, as delivery partner, and in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, as executing entity.

📸 Photos: UNICEF Maldives

featuredImage.alt: VilunVeshi School Garden Program Launched to Strengthen Climate Resilience and Food Security

en.title: VilunVeshi School Garden Program Launched to Strengthen Climate Resilience and Food Security
en.description: The Ministry of Tourism and Environment (MOTE) has officially launched the School Garden Program in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Welfare and the Ministry of Education. The program was launched during an orientation workshop held on 14th February 2026 at Meeruma, Malé.…
en.body:
The Ministry of Tourism and Environment (MOTE) has officially launched the School Garden Program in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Welfare and the Ministry of Education. The program was launched during an orientation workshop held on 14th February 2026 at Meeruma, Malé. The initiative is being implemented by the Climate Change Department of MOTE under the Enhancing Climate Resilience and Food Security Project (ECRFS).

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/MoTE-1024x819.jpg)

The workshop was officially inaugurated by Minister of State for Tourism and Environment, Mr. Ibrahim Mimrah, who highlighted the Ministry’s ongoing efforts to strengthen national food security in response to climate change challenges. He emphasized the importance of integrating urban agriculture into school systems by introducing diverse urban farming methods and fostering positive behavioural change among students. He further underscored the need to promote healthier school environments by prioritising nutritious food options such as fruits and vegetables.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/MoAAW-1024x819.jpg)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/MoE-1024x819.jpg)

Delivering the keynote address, Ministry of Education’s, Education Superintendent, Mr. Ismail Saudulla, stressed the importance of equipping students with practical knowledge and skills that connect classroom learning with real-world environmental challenges. He noted that school-based gardening initiatives can play a vital role in nurturing environmental stewardship, responsibility, and healthy lifestyle habits among young people.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Basheera-819x1024.jpg)

A total of 50 participants representing selected schools and relevant ministries involved in the initiative participated in the workshop. To initiate the program, three schools in the Greater Malé Area: Ghaazee School, Hiriya School, and Muhyidheen School have been selected. Preparatory work is currently underway to design and establish school gardens tailored to the specific interests and needs of each school. The program will subsequently be expanded to additional schools in later phases.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Muhyiddin-819x1024.jpg)

The program aims to promote hands-on learning related to the environment, climate change, and urban agriculture systems; enhance students’ awareness of nutrition and healthy food choices; build practical life skills through experiential learning; and encourage the adoption of climate-resilient and sustainable practices.

The objective of the ECRFS project is to reduce the vulnerability of Maldivian island communities to climate risks by strengthening both institutional and community capacities. Under Output 3 of the project, which focuses on promoting climate-smart technologies and practices within the agri-food system, the School Garden Program serves as a key activity. The project is funded through a combination of grants, loans, and technical assistance from the Asian Development Fund, the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific, the Ocean Resilience Coastal Adaptation Trust Fund, and the Government of Maldives.

dv.title: މޫސުމީ ބަދަލުތަކަށް ހޭނުމަށާއި ކާނާގެ ރައްކާތެރިކަން ކަށަވަރުކުރުމަށް “ވިލުންވެށި ސްކޫލް ގާޑަން ޕްރޮގްރާމް” އިފްތިތާޙްކޮށްފި
dv.description: މޫސުމީ ބަދަލުތަކުން ކުރިމަތިވާ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކާ ކުރިމަތިލުމަށާއި، ރާއްޖޭގެ ކާނާގެ ރައްކާތެރިކަން އިތުރުކުރުމުގެ މަގުސަދުގައި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ޓޫރިޒަމް އެންޑް އެންވަޔަރަންމަންޓް އިން “ވިލުންވެށި ސްކޫލް ގާޑަން ޕްރޮގްރާމް” ރަސްމީކޮށް އިފްތިތާޙްކޮށްފިއެވެ. މި ޕްރޮގްރާމް ކުރިއަށްގެންދަނީ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް…
dv.body:
މޫސުމީ ބަދަލުތަކުން ކުރިމަތިވާ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކާ ކުރިމަތިލުމަށާއި، ރާއްޖޭގެ ކާނާގެ ރައްކާތެރިކަން އިތުރުކުރުމުގެ މަގުސަދުގައި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ޓޫރިޒަމް އެންޑް އެންވަޔަރަންމަންޓް އިން “ވިލުންވެށި ސްކޫލް ގާޑަން ޕްރޮގްރާމް” ރަސްމީކޮށް އިފްތިތާޙްކޮށްފިއެވެ. މި ޕްރޮގްރާމް ކުރިއަށްގެންދަނީ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް އެގްރިކަލްޗަރ އެންޑް އެނިމަލް ވެލްފެއަރ އަދި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް އެޑިޔުކޭޝަން ގުޅިގެންނެވެ. މި ޕްރޮގްރާމް އިފްތިތާހުކޮށްފައިވަނީ  14 ފެބްރުއަރީ 2026  ގައި މީރުމާގައި ބޭއްވި އޮރިއެންޓޭޝަން ވޯކްޝޮޕްގައެވެ. މި މަސައްކަތަކީ މިނިސްޓްރީގެ ކްލައިމެޓް ޗޭންޖް ޑިޕާޓްމަންޓުން ކުރިއަށްގެންދާ “އެންހާންސިންގ ކްލައިމެޓް ރެސިލިއަންސް އެންޑް ފުޑް ސެކިއުރިޓީ” (ECRFS)  މަޝްރޫޢުގެ ދަށުން ގެންދާ ޕްރޮގްރާމެކެވެ.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/MoTE-1024x819.jpg)

މި މަސައްކަތު ބައްދަލުވުން ރަސްމީކޮށް އިފްތިތާޙްކޮށްދެއްވީ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ޓޫރިޒަމް އެންޑް އެންވަޔަރަންމަންޓްގެ ސްޓޭޓް މިނިސްޓަރ އަލްފާޟިލް އިބްރާހީމް މިމްރާހެވެ. މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުން މިމްރާހު ވިދާޅުވީ، މޫސުމީ ބަދަލުތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން ކުރިމަތިވާ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކަށް ބަލައި، ޤައުމީ ފެންވަރުގައި ކާނާގެ ރައްކާތެރިކަން ކަށަވަރުކުރުމަށް މިނިސްޓްރީން ގިނަ މަސައްކަތްތަކެއް ކުރަމުންދާ ކަމަށެވެ. އަދި މިފަދަ ޕްރޮގުރާމެއް ހިންގުމުގެ މައިގަޑު މަގުޞަދަކީ އާރބަން ސަރަޙައްދުތަކުގައި ދަނޑުވެރިކަން ކުރުމުގައި ބޭނުންކުރެވިދާނެ ތަފާތު ގޮތްތަކާއި، މިފަދަ ޕްރޮގުރާމުތަކަށް ސްކޫލުގެ މާހައުލުގައި ދަރިވަރުންގެ އާއި މުދައްރިސުންގެ ބައިވެރިވުން އިތުރުކުރުމަށް ކުރެވިދާނެ ކަންތަތްތަކާއި ސިއްޙަތައް ފައިދާކުރުވަނިވި ކާނާގެ ބާވަތްތައް ބޭނުންކުރުމަށް ބާރުވެރިކުރުމަށް އެޅިދާނެ ފިޔަވަޅުތައް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމެވެ.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/MoAAW-1024x819.jpg)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/MoE-1024x819.jpg)

މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ސްޓޭޓް ފޮރ އެގްރިކަލްޗަރ އެންޑް އެނިމަލް ވެލްފެއަރ ސްޓޭޓް މިނިސްޓަރ އަލްފާޟިލް އަޙްމަދު ދީދީ ވިދާޅުވީ، މޫސުމާ ރައްޓެހި ދަނޑުވެރި ކަމުގެ ޒަރީއްޔާ  ކާނާގެ ޔަގީންކަން އިތުރު ކުރުމަށާއި ތިމާވެށީގެ ހޭލުންތެރިކަން އިތުރުކޮށް ދަރިވަރުން ބައިވެރިކުރުމަކީ މުހިންމު ފިޔަވަޅެއްކަމަށް އަލިއަޅުއްވައިލެއްވިއެވެ. ސްޓޭޓް މިނިސްޓަރުގެ ވާހަކަފުޅުގައި، ކާބޯތަކެތީގެ ޔަގީންކަމަށް ކުރިމަތިވާ ގޮންޖެހުންތައް ޙައްލުކުރުމަށް އެކި ދާއިރާތަކުން އެކުގައި މަސައްކަތްކުރުމުގެ މުހިއްމުކަން ފާހަގަކުރައްވައި، މި ޕްރޮގުރާމު މެދުވެރިކޮށް މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން ކުރިމަތިވާ ނޭދެވޭ އަސަރުތަކަށް ހޭލުންތެރިކަން އިތުރުވެގެންދާނެކަމަށެވެ.

މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ޝަރަފުވެރި މެހެމާނު، މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް އެޑިޔުކޭޝަންގެ އެޑިޔުކޭޝަން ސުޕަރިންޓެންޑެންޓް، އަލްފާޟިލް އިސްމާޢީލް ސަޢުދުﷲ ވިދާޅުވީ، ކްލާސްރޫމްގައި އުނގަންނައިދޭ ތަޢުލީމާއި ތިމާވެށީގެ ޙަޤީޤީ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކާ ގުޅުވައިދޭނެ ފަދަ ޢަމަލީ ހުނަރުތަކާއި މަޢުލޫމާތު ދަރިވަރުންނަށް ފޯރުކޮށްދިނުމަކީ ނުހަނު ބޭނުންތެރި ކަމެއް ކަމަށެވެ. ސްކޫލްތަކުގައި ހިންގޭ މިފަދަ ދަނޑުވެރިކަމުގެ ހަރަކާތްތަކަކީ ތިމާވެށި ރައްކާތެރިކުރުމުގެ ރޫޙާއި، ޒިންމާދާރުކަން އަދި ދަރިވަރުންގެ ދުޅަހެޔޮކަން އިތުރުކުރުމުގައި މުހިންމު ދައުރެއް އަދާކުރާނެ ކަމެއްކަންވެސް ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Basheera-819x1024.jpg)

މި ވޯކްޝޮޕްގައި، މި ޕްރޮގްރާމްގައި ހިމެނޭ މިނިސްޓްރީތަކާއި ހޮވާލެވުނު ސްކޫލްތަކުން ޖުމްލަ 50 ބައިވެރިން ބައިވެރިވިއެވެ. މި ޕްރޮގްރާމްގެ ފުރަތަމަ މަރުޙަލާ ފެށުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވަނީ ގްރޭޓަރ މާލެ ސަރަޙައްދުގެ ތިން ސްކޫލެއްގައެވެ. އެއީ ޣާޒީ ސްކޫލް، ހިރިޔާ ސްކޫލް އަދި މުޙްޔިއްދީން ސްކޫލެވެ. މިމަސައްކަތު ބައްދަލުވުމުގެ ނަތީޖާއެއްގެ ގޮތުން މިފަދަ ޕްރޮގުރާމުތައް މެދުނުކެޑި ސްކޫލުތަކުގައި ހިންގޭނެ ދުރު ރާސްތާ ޕްލޭނެއް ތައްޔާރުކުރެވިގެންދާނެއެވެ. މީގެ އިތުރުން، އާރބަން ސަރަޙައްދުތަކުގައި ދަނޑުވެރިކަން ކުރުމުގައި ބޭނުންކުރެވިދާނެ ތަފާތު ގޮތްތަކާއި، މިފަދަ ޕްރޮގުރާމުތަކަށް ސްކޫލުގެ މާހައުލުގައި ދަރިވަރުންގެ އާއި މުދައްރިސުންގެ ބައިވެރިވުން އިތުރުކުރުމަށް ކުރެވިދާނެ ކަންތަތްތަކާއި ސިއްޙަތައް ފައިދާކުރުވަނިވި ކާނާގެ ބާވަތްތައް ބޭނުންކުރުމަށް ބާރުވެރިކުރުމަށް އެޅިދާނެ ފިޔަވަޅުތައް މަޝްވަރާކުރެވުނެވެ.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Muhyiddin-819x1024.jpg)

“އެންހާންސިންގ ކްލައިމެޓް ރެސިލިއަންސް އެންޑް ފުޑް ސެކިއުރި “(ECRFS)  މަޝްރޫޢުގެ ލަނޑުދަނޑި ތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި މޫސުމީ ބަދަލުތަކާ ގުޅިގެން އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކަށް ތައްޔާރުވުމަށް މުއައްސަސާތަކާއި މުޖުތަމަޢުގެ ޤާބިލުކަން އިތުރުކުރުމާއި، ޤުދުރަތީ ވަޞީލަތްތައް ބޭނުންކޮށްގެން ފެންބޮޑުވުމާއި އުދައެރުމުން ރައްކާތެރިވުމަށް އެކަށީގެންވާ ފިޔަވަޅުތައް އެޅުމުގެ އިތުރުން ދަނޑުވެރިކަމާއި ކާބޯތަކެތީގެ ނިޒާމުތަކުގައި މޫސުމީ ބަދަލުތަކަށް އެކަށޭނަ ޓެކްނޮލޮޖީތަކާއި އާދަތައް ތަޢާރަފުކުރުން އަދި މޫސުމީ ބަދަލުތަކަށް ތައްޔާރުވުމަށް ކުރެވޭ ވިޔަފާރިތަކާއި ޚިދުމަތްތައް އިތުރުކުރުމާއި، ދަނޑުވެރިކަން ކުރިއެރުވުން ހިމެނެއެވެ.

featuredImage.alt: Second Stakeholder Consultation Workshop on National Carbon Regulation Held

en.title: Second Stakeholder Consultation Workshop on National Carbon Regulation Held
en.description: The Climate Change Department (CCD) of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment convened the second stakeholder consultation workshop on the development of a National Carbon Regulation on 12 February 2026 at Meeruma, Malé. The consultation was held to present and discuss the first draft of the…
en.body:
The Climate Change Department (CCD) of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment convened the second stakeholder consultation workshop on the development of a National Carbon Regulation on 12 February 2026 at Meeruma, Malé. The consultation was held to present and discuss the first draft of the regulation, bringing together key government institutions, sectoral stakeholders, and technical experts.

The workshop opened with remarks by Minister of State Mr. Ibrahim Mimrah. In his address, he emphasized that climate change is a global challenge requiring coordinated international action, with many countries undertaking meaningful measures to address its impacts. He highlighted that the proposed National Carbon Regulation will support cooperative approaches toward achieving the Maldives’ Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) targets, while creating an enabling environment for credible buyers, high-integrity carbon credits, and robust NDC accounting.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260212-pic-Second-Carbon-Workshop-3.png)

A technical presentation was delivered by Ms. Fathimath Raufa Moosa, Project Technical Coordinator, Climate Change Department. Participants were briefed on the policy context underpinning the regulation, including current national climate targets, reporting obligations, and risks associated with unregulated carbon activities. The session also outlined strategic opportunities related to technology transfer, capacity building, and climate finance mobilisation through well-governed carbon market engagement.

This was followed by the presentation of the first draft of the regulation by Development Advisory Services (D.A.S.) Pvt Ltd. The draft outlined proposed institutional arrangements, procedures for authorisation of carbon activities and tracking and reporting mechanisms.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260212-pic-Second-Carbon-Workshop.png)

A total of 43 participants took part in the workshop. Representatives attended from the President’s Office, Ministry of Cities, Local Governments and Public Works, Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation, State Electric Company Limited, Maldives Transport and Contracting Company, Attorney General’s Office, Maldives Civil Aviation Authority, Islamic University of Maldives, State Trading Organization, Maldives Airports Company Limited, Maldives Finance and Leasing Company Pvt Ltd, Invest Maldives, the Environmental Regulatory Authority, and the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Welfare. Officials from the Climate Change Department, Ozone Unit, and Legal Unit of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment also participated, along with representatives from sectoral NGOs and independent experts.

The presentation was followed by constructive discussions, with participants raising questions and providing comments on various aspects of the draft regulation. The workshop concluded with the Ministry expressing appreciation to all participants for their active engagement and valuable contributions, which will inform further refinement of the draft National Carbon Regulation.

featuredImage.alt: Maldives Advances Climate Finance Coordination Through GCF Country Pipeline Initial Ideation Workshop

en.title: Maldives Advances Climate Finance Coordination Through GCF Country Pipeline Initial Ideation Workshop
en.description: The Climate Change Department (CCD) of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment successfully convened the Maldives Country Pipeline to the Green Climate Fund: Initial Project Ideation Discussion Workshop on 11 February 2026, bringing together line ministries and key government agencies to strengthen…
en.body:
The Climate Change Department (CCD) of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment successfully convened the Maldives Country Pipeline to the Green Climate Fund: Initial Project Ideation Discussion Workshop on 11 February 2026, bringing together line ministries and key government agencies to strengthen national coordination on climate finance planning.

The one-day inter-ministerial workshop marked an important step in advancing the Maldives’ efforts to translate national climate priorities into well-structured, coordinated, and bankable project and programme concepts suitable for mobilisation of international climate finance, including from the Green Climate Fund (GCF).

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260211-pic-GCF-Interministerial-workshop.png)

The workshop was held in the context of the Maldives’ Third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), the ongoing National Adaptation Plan (NAP) development process, and national submissions to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), which collectively outline the country’s priority sectors and cross-cutting climate challenges. Participants engaged in structured discussions to reaffirm sectoral priorities, identify potential project ideas, and explore opportunities for cross-sectoral and programmatic approaches.

The workshop was officially opened by Mr. Ibrahim Mimrah, Minister of State for Tourism and Environment. In his opening remarks, the State Minister Mimrah emphasised that updating the national climate finance project pipeline is a strategic priority, noting that the pipeline is intended not merely as a list of project ideas, but as a tool to help prioritise, sequence, and align climate investments across sectors and institutions. He also highlighted the importance of inter-ministerial collaboration and institutional ownership in developing a strong, nationally anchored pipeline that can support future engagement with climate funds and development partners.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260211-pic-GCF-Interministerial-workshop-2.png)

Participants were first given a scene-setting presentation by Ms. Fathimath Zaina Shareef, GCF Laision Officer, to provide context on the GCF country pipeline, climate finance mobilisation efforts and relevance to Maldives’ third NDC. The workshop was carried out through a participatory and facilitation-led approach, with interactive breakout sessions enabling ministries and agencies to articulate climate-relevant project and programme concepts within their respective mandates, while identifying synergies and complementarities across sectors. Discussions also focused on practical next steps for further concept development, including follow-up actions and information needs.

Key outcomes of the workshop included the identification of priority climate project ideas, initial mapping of lead and supporting institutions, recognition of cross-sectoral linkages, and agreement on next steps to further strengthen the national climate finance project pipeline.

To close the workshop, Mr. Ahmed Waheed, Director of the Climate Change Department noted that the outcomes of the workshop will contribute directly to ongoing efforts to strengthen a coherent, whole-of-government approach to climate finance planning and enhance the Maldives’ readiness to mobilise international climate finance for long-term, impactful climate action.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260211-pic-GCF-Interministerial-workshop-5.png)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260211-pic-GCF-Interministerial-workshop-4.png)

en.title: Inception Workshop Held to Initiate the Development of Maldives’ First Climate Change Gender Action Plan
en.description: The Climate Change Department (CCD) of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment conducted an inception workshop on 26 January 2026 to initiate the development of the Maldives’ first Climate Change Gender Action Plan (CC-GAP). The workshop was held at Meerumaa and brought together 32 participants…
en.body:
The Climate Change Department (CCD) of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment conducted an inception workshop on 26 January 2026 to initiate the development of the Maldives’ first Climate Change Gender Action Plan (CC-GAP). The workshop was held at Meerumaa and brought together 32 participants from government ministries and civil society organizations.

The workshop was officially opened by Ibrahim Mimrah, Minister of State for Tourism and Environment, who highlighted the Ministry’s ongoing efforts to strengthen national climate action through the development of key frameworks and reporting instruments, including the National Adaptation Plan and the implementation of the Maldives’ Third Nationally Determined Contribution.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20260126-pic-Gender-Action-Plan-Inception-8.png)

Following the opening remarks, Thibyan Ibrahim, Director of the Climate Change Department, provided an overview of the objectives of the workshop. He outlined the current work being undertaken by the Department to strengthen climate governance and coordination, and noted that the CC-GAP will serve as a dedicated framework to systematically integrate gender considerations into climate adaptation and mitigation planning, implementation, and monitoring processes.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20260126-pic-Gender-Action-Plan-Inception-4.png)

The workshop was facilitated by Jauza Khaleel, Senior Climate Change Adaptation Consultant. Through technical presentations and facilitated group discussions, participants examined the gender and climate change nexus in the Maldives, including gender-differentiated climate vulnerabilities and capacities, and identified key gaps in existing climate policies and actions. Participants also worked collaboratively to develop a preliminary conceptual framework and to identify and prioritise gender-responsive climate actions across key sectors, providing inputs that will inform the structure, priorities, and implementation approach of the Climate Change Gender Action Plan.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20260126-pic-Gender-Action-Plan-Inception-9.png)

The workshop was attended by representatives from the President’s Office – Special Envoy for Climate Change, the Ministry of Cities, Local Government and Public Works, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology, the Environment Protection Authority, the Ministry of Finance and Planning, the Maldives Meteorological Services, the Ministry of Social and Family Development, the Attorney General’s Office, Small Island Geographic Society, Society for Health Education, Maldives Authentic Crafts Cooperative Society, Maldives Red Crescent, Maldives National University, Islamic University Maldives, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF).

The CC-GAP is being developed by the Climate Change Department with technical assistance from the NAP Global Network.

featuredImage.alt: British High Commissioner Meets Climate Change Department to Discuss Climate Finance and Loss and Damage Response

en.title: British High Commissioner Meets Climate Change Department to Discuss Climate Finance and Loss and Damage Response
en.description: The Climate Change Department held a meeting with representatives of the British High Commission in Malé at the request of the British High Commissioner to discuss cooperation on climate finance, with a particular focus on the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) and broader technical…
en.body:
The Climate Change Department held a meeting with representatives of the British High Commission in Malé at the request of the British High Commissioner to discuss cooperation on climate finance, with a particular focus on the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) and broader technical assistance needs of the Maldives.

During the meeting, Director General of the Climate Change Department Amjad Abdulla provided updates on ongoing internal discussions regarding the Barbados Implementation Modalities (BIM) of the FRLD. The Climate Change Department highlighted that the Maldives has long advocated for greater international support to address slow onset climate impacts, while also recognising that rapid onset and extreme weather events may require immediate attention, particularly in areas such as flood mitigation and coastal protection.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20260119-pic-British-High-Commision-3.png)

In discussions on implementation arrangements, the Ministry highlighted one of the key challenges faced by the Maldives in accessing international climate finance being the absence of nationally accredited direct access entities to multilateral climate funds. The Ministry emphasised the importance of continued support to address this structural constraint while supporting matchmaking efforts with international partners for the development and implementation of climate projects.

The Climate Change Department further underscored the critical importance of direct budget support to governments in the context of loss and damage response, as the feature which sets the FRLD apart from other climate funds. The Climate Change Department reiterated its intention to continue advocating for the operationalisation of this instrument, alongside other developing countries, and expressed its hope for support from the United Kingdom in this regard, including through its representation on relevant boards.

The Climate Change Department also raised broader areas of cooperation, including ongoing engagement with the Green Climate Fund (GCF), the Maldives’ bid to host a GCF Regional Office, and the importance of support from the UK’s board members representing the Foreign, Development and Commonwealth Office.

In addition, the Climate Change Department conveyed its appreciation for the work of the Commonwealth Secretariat and the Commonwealth Climate Finance Access Hub, and expressed its interest in continued support from the Commonwealth to strengthen access to climate finance and technical assistance.

The meeting reaffirmed the positive role played by the United Kingdom in international climate processes. The Climate Change Department reiterated its commitment to continued engagement with UK negotiators, board members, and institutions, and to strengthening collaboration in support of the Maldives’ climate priorities.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20260119-pic-British-High-Commision-2.png)

featuredImage.alt: Ministry Signs Contract to Supply Double-Cab Vehicle for Hanimadhoo Agriculture Centre

en.title: Ministry Signs Contract to Supply Double-Cab Vehicle for Hanimadhoo Agriculture Centre
en.description: The Ministry of Tourism and Environment (MoTE) has signed a contract with SAS MA Pvt Ltd for the supply and delivery of a double-cab vehicle to the Hanimadhoo Agriculture Centre (HAC) to improve operational efficiency of the center. This is being carried out by the Climate Change Department under…
en.body:
The Ministry of Tourism and Environment (MoTE) has signed a contract with SAS MA Pvt Ltd for the supply and delivery of a double-cab vehicle to the Hanimadhoo Agriculture Centre (HAC) to improve operational efficiency of the center. This is being carried out by the Climate Change Department under the Enhancing Climate Resilience and Food Security Project (ECRFS).

The agreement was signed on behalf of the Ministry by the Permanent Secretary, Mr. Ajwad Musthafa, and on behalf of the supplier by the Managing Director of SAS MA Pvt Ltd, Ms. Mariyam Madheeha. The Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Welfare, Mr. Mohamed Anees, also participated in the signing event.

The procurement of the vehicle forms part of broader efforts under the ECRFS project to strengthen operational capacities at the Hanimadhoo Agriculture Centre. Under Output 3 of the project, which focuses on the promotion of climate-smart technologies and practices in the agri-food system, the ECRFS project supports the construction and development of a multi-purpose facility at the Centre. Planned developments include a training space, a basic laboratory for soil and plant pathogen testing, and office facilities. These infrastructure upgrades will be complemented by capacity-building activities such as training for farmers and urban home gardeners, provision of technical advisory services for urban farming and agribusinesses, operation of an advisory clinic, and the upgrading of demonstration plots.

The main objective of the project is to reduce the vulnerability of Maldivian island communities to climate risks by strengthening institutional and community capacities. The project is funded through a combination of grants, loans, and technical assistance from the Asian Development Fund, the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific, the Ocean Resilience Coastal Adaptation Trust Fund, and the Government of Maldives.

Key components of the project include the installation of a weather radar system in Addu and the repair of the existing system in Malé; implementation of effective flood and coastal protection measures through nature-based solutions in Hdh. Kulhudhufushi; promotion of climate-smart technologies and practices within the agri-food system; and support for climate adaptation businesses and urban farming through a grant-matching scheme.

The session was organised to strengthen awareness on climate action and climate diplomacy,…
en.body:
The Climate Change Department in collaboration with the Foreign Service Institute of Maldives (FOSIM), conducted a climate change briefing session for Maldivian diplomats of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The session was organised to strengthen awareness on climate action and climate diplomacy, and to build the capacity of Maldivian missions and embassies abroad in advancing the Maldives’ climate change priorities.

The session started with a statement by Minister of Tourism and Environment H.E. Thoriq Ibrahim, who highlighted the critical importance of strong collaboration between the Ministry and the Foreign Service in representing the Maldives. He noted that diplomats play an essential role as the external voice of the Maldives, ensuring that national interests, including on climate change, are heard and understood in bilateral and multilateral forums. Minister Thoriq further noted that while diplomats work across a wide range of issues, climate change diplomacy requires coordinated messaging led by technical experts to avoid inconsistencies and ensure credibility in negotiations.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20251230-pic-climate_change_briefing_diplomats.png)

During the technical presentation, Director General Amjad Abdulla provided diplomats with an overview of the international climate change policy regime and the latest developments under the UNFCCC process, including the outcomes of recent climate change conferences, the Global Mutirão of COP30, the Global Goal on Adaptation, and climate finance priorities. The presentation also highlighted the Maldives’ Climate Action Plan (also referred to as Maldives’ Third Nationally Determined Contribution), ongoing adaptation and mitigation initiatives, and the country’s continued leadership in advocating for the needs of small island developing States. The session also underscored the importance of disciplined coordination on cross-cutting thematic areas such as security, sustainable development and human rights.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20251230-pic-climate_change_briefing_diplomats-3.png)

The session further discussed the strategic importance of strengthening Maldives’ presence in regional and international climate change institutions, including ongoing efforts to enhance engagement with the Green Climate Fund and other climate action mechanisms, to support national resilience, energy security and sustainable development priorities.

Diplomats participating in the session expressed appreciation for the opportunity to deepen their understanding of climate change policy and implementation priorities and reaffirmed their commitment to supporting national climate change diplomacy through their work in overseas missions.

en.title: First Stakeholder Consultation Workshop on National Carbon Regulation Held
en.description: The Climate Change Department (CCD) of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment convened the first stakeholder consultation workshop on the development of a National Carbon Regulation on 21 December 2025 at Champa Central Hotel, Malé. The consultation was conducted as a technical meeting, bringing…
en.body:
The Climate Change Department (CCD) of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment convened the first stakeholder consultation workshop on the development of a National Carbon Regulation on 21 December 2025 at Champa Central Hotel, Malé. The consultation was conducted as a technical meeting, bringing together key government institutions and sectoral stakeholders to provide initial inputs into the regulatory framework for managing national carbon activities in the Maldives.

The workshop opened with remarks by Mr. Amjad Abdulla, Director General of the Climate Change Department, who highlighted the growing importance of establishing a clear and robust national framework to govern carbon-related activities. He emphasized the need to safeguard national interests, ensure environmental integrity, and position the Maldives to responsibly access emerging climate finance opportunities linked to carbon markets.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/20251221-pic-National_Carbon_Regulation-3.png)

During the technical sessions, participants were briefed on the need for a National Carbon Regulation, including current gaps and risks associated with unregulated carbon activities, as well as the strategic opportunities for climate finance mobilisation and participation in international carbon markets. Presentations also outlined the proposed direction for developing the regulation, particularly in the context of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and the management of mitigation outcomes.

The latter part of the workshop focused on facilitated group discussions, where stakeholders exchanged views on institutional roles and responsibilities, carbon market processes, risk management, and safeguards. Inputs from these discussions will inform the drafting of a regulation that is not overly complex, builds on existing institutional arrangements, and establishes clear procedures for authorisation, tracking, and reporting of carbon-related activities.

This workshop marks the first in a series of consultations planned under the National Carbon Regulation development process. Further stakeholder engagement opportunities will be conducted as the draft regulation is prepared and refined.

en.title: Workshop on Tourism Statistics Survey Conducted
en.description: The Maldives Bureau of Statistics (MBS), with support from the Ministry of Tourism and Environment (MOTE), conducted a Workshop on the Tourism Statistics Survey on 17th December 2025 in Malé. Tourism is a key sector of the Maldivian economy, contributing significantly to national income,…
en.body:
The Maldives Bureau of Statistics (MBS), with support from the Ministry of Tourism and Environment (MOTE), conducted a Workshop on the Tourism Statistics Survey on 17th December 2025 in Malé. Tourism is a key sector of the Maldivian economy, contributing significantly to national income, employment, and foreign investment. As an energy-intensive sector, tourism also plays an important role in national climate change mitigation efforts, particularly in improving the availability and quality of data required for greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory preparation.

At the opening ceremony, State Minister Ibrahim Mimrah of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment highlighted the importance of strengthening energy-related data from the tourism sector to support evidence-based policymaking, national GHG inventory development, and international climate reporting.

To strengthen inter-agency collaboration and improve sector-specific energy data, the Ministry of Tourism and Environment, Maldives Bureau of Statistics, and the Utility Regulatory Authority (URA) signed a Memorandum of Understanding on 6 November 2024. With support from the Capacity Building for Improved Transparency of Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation Actions in the Maldives (CBIT Maldives) project, the Tourism Statistics Survey form was enhanced to include additional energy-related data.

The updated Tourism Statistics Survey 2024, launched in December 2024, expands the scope of data collected from tourism establishments by introducing new energy consumption modules, alongside existing sections on human resources, finance, and operations. These enhancements aim to address historical data gaps and support the integration of tourism sector data into national GHG inventories, in line with reporting requirements under the Enhanced Transparency Framework of the Paris Agreement.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/20251217-pic-Tourism_Statistics_Survey-9.png)

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/20251217-pic-Tourism_Statistics_Survey-8.png)

The workshop focused on disseminating the updates made to the survey form, presenting key findings from the 2023 Tourism Statistics Survey, and providing a section-by-section overview of the 2024 survey form. A presentation on the overview of the national GHG inventory and the role of the tourism sector was delivered by Ahmed Masoon, Programme Officer from the Climate Change Department of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment. The presentation outlined how tourism sector energy data contributes to national emissions estimates and supports transparency and reporting obligations.

A total of 30 participants  took part in the workshop. The workshop was attended by representatives from tourism establishments including Constance Moofushi Resort, Atmosphere Kanifushi Resort, Coco Collection (operating Coco Bodu Hithi Resort and Coco Palm Dhuni Kolhu), Embudu Village Resort, Waldorf Astoria Maldives Ithaafushi, Bathala Resort, and Baros Maldives. Representatives from key industry associations, including the Maldives Association of Travel Agents and Tour Operators and the Maldives Association of Tourism Industry, also participated, supporting broader engagement with the tourism sector. Officials from the Climate Change Department and Tourism Department of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment, Waste Management Corporation Limited, and the Maldives Bureau of Statistics attended the workshop.

The Tourism Statistics Survey 2024 is currently underway, and resorts, hotels, guesthouses, and safari vessels are requested to submit their survey responses through the official online platform at:
🔗 <https://tourismsurvey.stats.gov.mv/>

The CBIT Maldives project is funded by the Global Environment Facility and implemented by the Ministry of Tourism and Environment with support from the United Nations Environment Programme.

en.description: The Climate Change Department (CCD) of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment (MOTE) successfully conducted a Training on Tools & Methodologies for Tracking Mitigation Actions on 8th December 2025 at Meeruma, Male’.
en.body:
The Climate Change Department (CCD) of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment (MOTE) successfully conducted a Training on Tools & Methodologies for Tracking Mitigation Actions on 8th December 2025 at Meeruma, Male’.

The workshop was organized under the Capacity Strengthening for Improved Transparency of Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation Actions in the Maldives (CBIT Maldives) project, funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and supported by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). The training was delivered by Riyan Private Limited, in association with Grant Thornton Bharat LLP.

![](https://old.environment.gov.mv/v2/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/20251208-pic-Training_Mitigation_Actions-4.png)

The session introduced participants to indicators and methodologies developed for tracking mitigation actions, as well as standardized reporting formats to strengthen transparent and consistent national reporting. Participants engaged in guided exercises and practical demonstrations to enhance their understanding of data requirements and reporting processes.

A total of 16  participants (9 male, 7 female) attended the workshop, representing key national stakeholders involved in mitigation data collection and reporting. Participants included representatives from Maldives Ports Limited (MPL), Male’ Water and Sewerage Company (MWSC), the Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation, Waste Management Corporation (WAMCO), State Electric Company Limited (STELCO), the President’s Office, and Maldives Airports Company Limited (MACL). Officials from the Climate Change Department, Energy Department, and Ozone Unit of the Ministry of Tourism and Environment also took part in the training sessions.
